headline: Margins expand and debt is paid off, but growth stays flat
summary_short: Teradata's Q2 2026 total revenue was flat y/y at $410M as 3% recurring-revenue growth was offset by a 24% consulting-services decline; GAAP operating margin expanded 580bps to 11.7% and the company fully repaid its $450M term loan, ending the quarter debt-free with $414M cash.
summary_long: Recurring revenue (+3% y/y, 89% of total) and total ARR (+1% reported, led by public cloud ARR +8%) grew, but a 24% consulting-services drop left total revenue flat. GAAP gross margin rose to 59.3% (+290bps) and operating margin to 11.7% (+580bps) on lower SG&A. Net income and diluted EPS jumped y/y (2.1% tax rate vs 30.8%) but fell sharply q/q since Q1 2026 booked a one-time $381M SAP settlement gain. The company used $450M of operating cash to repay all long-term debt, ending the quarter debt-free with $414M cash. Teradata raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to $2.65-$2.73, GAAP EPS to $4.43-$4.51, cash flow from operations to $665-$685M, and adjusted free cash flow to $330-$350M, while reaffirming FY2026 ARR/revenue growth ranges.

drivers.explanation: Recurring-revenue and public-cloud ARR growth plus lower SG&A drove GAAP and non-GAAP margin expansion; the company raised full-year non-GAAP EPS and adjusted free cash flow guidance and used the quarter's cash flow to retire all long-term debt.
Public cloud ARR rose 8% as reported (9% constant-currency) to $686M, the release's cited driver of total ARR growth to $1,509M.
Recurring revenue +3% and perpetual licenses/hardware +167% (off a small $3M base) were offset by consulting services falling 24% to $39M, netting to flat total revenue.
Mix shift toward higher-margin product revenue (66.8% segment gross margin) versus consulting services (-5.1% segment gross margin) lifted total gross margin to 59.3% from 56.4%.
SG&A fell to $120M from $135M even as R&D rose to $75M from $71M; the release does not further explain the SG&A decline.
Higher operating income, a smaller other-expense line (-$1M vs -$11M), and a GAAP effective tax rate of 2.1% versus 30.8% a year ago drove net income up 411% y/y.

The 86% sequential drop reflects Q1 2026's one-time $3.72/share SAP litigation settlement benefit (six-month GAAP EPS was $3.95 versus $0.48 for Q2 alone), not a change in underlying operating performance.
Higher net income and a $66M favorable swing in receivables collections (versus +$14M a year ago) lifted operating cash flow to $106M from $43M.
Tracks the operating cash flow improvement; management's reconciliation excludes the SAP settlement's cash effects from this non-GAAP measure.
The company repaid $450M of long-term borrowings during the quarter, per the cash flow statement's financing activities, retiring all long-term debt.
The sequential cash decline is fully explained by the $450M debt repayment funded from the prior quarter's elevated cash balance.
